look_here_first: CHECK THE BASE FIRST: short HARD KNOTTY RHIZOMES with beadlike/bud swellings, rather than an annual purely fibrous root. Then examine a short packed bristly head (often 2.5–7 cm) and COUNT the MANY bristles near each spikelet—commonly ~6–7, sometimes 4–12. Check the true membranous plus hairy ligule (~0.5–1.3 mm).

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. pumila (yellow foxtail, outside the four canonical cards) can resemble the short yellowish head, but it is ordinarily an annual without knotty rhizomes; field color alone is worthless. S. scheelei also has a perennial base but usually a substantially longer head and roughly one long bristle per spikelet. S. reverchonii has a looser often interrupted head and short sparse bristles, unlike the multiple bristles here.
diagnostic_sequence: Inspect the basal rootstock for short hard knotty rhizomes; do not uproot protected or sensitive plants.
Use a hand lens on spikelets: several bristles at each base; spikelets approximately 2–3 mm.
Photograph leaf ligule and a complete plant habit; existing single macro does not show the decisive rhizome.

best_field_traits: Perennial with firm short knotty rhizomes, to about 4 cm in a local Texas botanical treatment, sometimes with swollen buds at shoot bases.
Stem nodes often bent (geniculate); short densely bristly cylindrical flowering heads commonly 25–70 mm.
Many sterile bristles grouped beneath each spikelet: usually six or seven, observed local-treatment range about four to twelve.
Spikelets about 2.2–2.5 mm long; no floret awns (bristles are sterile reduced branchlets).
Thin blades frequently about 2–4.5 mm broad, with a mixed membranous/hairy true ligule roughly 0.5–1.3 mm.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Same rooted mature plant: clump plus inflorescence
Exposed hard knotty rhizomes with buds and 1-cm ruler (rehabilitate soil after photo)
Single attached spikelet with COUNTABLE 4–12 basal bristles at ≥10x
Collar ligule side-on and spikelet/glume mm macro
crew_field_check: Count bristles under 10× magnification; these are reduced branches, NOT true awns.
Measure whole flowering head and a mature spikelet.
Inspect the base/collar/rhizomes on the SAME PLANT; do not force identification from a single image.
